gui.cobbledollarscommandshops.admin.help: Choose which operations are written to the server log. This data also powers /cdshops stats.
Configure the messages and sounds sent to players after a purchase, sale or access denial.
Message shown when a player does not meet this shop's conditions. If absent or empty, the default denial message is used.
Conditions at this level are combined with those of parent levels. All configured condition groups must pass; an empty list adds no restriction.
Organize offers into named groups, each with its own optional access conditions. Use the arrows to change their order.
Category name shown to players. It must contain at least one character.
Offers in this category or bank. Edit their items, prices and conditions; use the arrows to change their order.
Offer identifier, unique across the shop, used for stock tracking and commands. Use a–z, 0–9, _ or -; changing it may affect stock tracking.
Choose which items this offer applies to. An item must match at least one inclusion rule and no exclusion rule.
Add at least one rule defining accepted items. Rules can target an item, an item with components, a tag or all items from a mod.
Remove items from this offer's inclusion rules. Within this offer, an exclusion takes precedence over an inclusion; another offer can introduce the item again.
Registered item identifier, for example minecraft:stone. In a matching rule, the item's components are ignored.
Item definition using Minecraft command syntax, including optional components. Matching takes these components into account.
Existing item tag, for example minecraft:logs, with or without #. The rule applies to all items in that tag.
Namespace of the items to include, for example cobblemon. It must match at least one registered item.
Number of items given per purchased bundle. Must be a positive integer; defaults to 1.
CobbleDollars charged for one purchased bundle, regardless of its item count. Must be a non-negative integer; 0 makes it free.
Maximum bundles each player can buy from this offer. -1 means unlimited, 0 makes it unavailable; restocking requires finite stock.
Automatically replenish each player's stock at real-time intervals or at a daily time. Stock never exceeds this offer's configured capacity.
Regular interval: add a number of bundles at each interval. Daily reset: restore full stock at the chosen real-world time.
Bundles added to stock at each interval, up to its capacity. Must be a positive integer.
Real-time delay between restocks, in seconds. Must be a positive integer; 3600 means one hour.
Real-world hour for restoring full stock, from 0 to 23, in the selected time zone.
Minute of the daily full restock, from 0 to 59. Defaults to 0.
Time zone for the daily reset, for example Europe/Paris or UTC. If absent, the server's time zone is used.
Extra rewards given for groups of bundles bought in one transaction. Multiple bonuses can apply together.
Bundles required in one transaction for one set of rewards. Example: threshold 3, purchase of 7 bundles = 2 sets; the threshold must be positive and cannot exceed finite stock.
Items given each time the bonus threshold is reached within a purchase. Add at least one reward and its quantity.
The player must have every tag in this list, assigned with /tag. Names are case-sensitive.
The player must have at least one tag from this list, assigned with /tag. An empty list adds no requirement.
Access is denied if the player has any of these tags. Use the same names as in the /tag command.
The player must have completed all listed advancements. Use their identifiers, for example minecraft:story/root.
The player must have completed at least one listed advancement. An empty list adds no requirement.
The player must be in one of these dimensions, for example minecraft:overworld. An empty list allows all dimensions.
World time must fall within at least one range. A day has 24000 ticks; a range whose start exceeds its end wraps into the next day.
Inclusive range start, from 0 to 23999 ticks. 0 means 6 AM and 12000 means 6 PM; start and end must differ.
Exclusive range end, from 0 to 23999 ticks. If lower than the start, the range continues into the next day.
Every configured score condition must pass. A missing objective or a player without a score fails the condition.
Internal scoreboard objective name, as used with /scoreboard objectives. It must exist and the player must have a score in it.
Minimum allowed score, inclusive. Combined with the maximum and exact-value constraints when configured.
Maximum allowed score, inclusive. Combined with the minimum and exact-value constraints when configured.
The player's score must equal this integer exactly. Any configured minimum or maximum must also be satisfied.
Applies to successful purchases. In player feedback, configures messages and sounds; in audit settings, enables logging.
Applies to failed purchases, such as insufficient funds or stock. In player feedback, configures messages and sounds; in audit settings, enables logging.
Applies to successful sales to the bank. In player feedback, configures messages and sounds; in audit settings, enables logging.
Applies to failed sale attempts. In player feedback, configures messages and sounds; in audit settings, enables logging.
Messages and sounds sent when access to a shop is denied. Default channels are chat and sound.
Logs shop enable and disable operations performed through commands.
Choose how to notify the player: action bar, chat or sound. An empty list disables all feedback for this event; the sound channel is required to play the sound.
Sound played for this event when the sound channel is enabled. No sound disables it; removing the setting restores the event's default sound.
Volume of the sound played to the player. A small value such as 0.25 is quiet; if absent, the event's default volume is used.
Sound pitch: higher values make the sound higher-pitched. If absent, the event's default pitch is used.
Enables or disables all audit logging. Individual event types can be configured separately.
Flushes each event to the log file immediately. Disabling it allows buffered writes, but recent entries may be lost if the server stops abruptly.
Choose which operation types to keep in the log. These switches only apply while audit logging is enabled.
Choose a plain item, an item with components, a tag or all items from a mod. Changing this type replaces the rule being edited.
No sound disables playback; identifier only uses the event's default volume and pitch. Detailed format lets you set both values.
Categories group offers and allow conditions per group. A simple list keeps all offers at one level; remove category conditions before converting to it.
Add an entry, then edit its settings. In an ordered list, arrows move the entry, + duplicates it and − deletes it.
Filters the list by name or identifier. Press Enter or leave the field to apply your text; clear the search to show all entries.
Edit this entry's value. The server validates the complete configuration when you save.
CobbleDollars paid to the player for each item sold to the bank. Must be a non-negative integer; this price is per item, regardless of stack size.
Items given for one occurrence of this reward. Must be a positive integer; multiplied by the number of bonus thresholds reached in the purchase.
Registered sound identifier, for example minecraft:entity.experience_orb.pickup. The sound must be known to the server.
Configure this shop's access conditions, categories and purchase offers. Changes take effect after saving.
Configure which items players can sell and their buyback prices. A local bank applies to its shop; the global bank is used when no local bank is defined.
